title: AI is flooding bug bounties. Microsoft paid a record; Apple slammed the door
excerpt: Apple capped its bug bounty over a flood of AI-generated reports the same week Microsoft paid a record $20m. Google repriced to reward the hard bugs.
content_html:
AI has learned to find software bugs faster than people can, and the programmes that pay for them are straining. In a single week, the three biggest went three different ways.

Microsoft paid out a record sum. Apple slammed the door on how many bugs a researcher can file. Google quietly repriced the whole thing. All three were reacting to the same flood.

Microsoft paid more than $20m to 562 researchers over its latest bounty year, The Register reported, a record on both counts. A year earlier it was about $17m to 344. Microsoft blamed the “growing use of AI” in security research for the surge.

But it is not a clean comparison: the company also widened what counts as a bug halfway through the year.

Apple slams the door

Apple went the opposite way. It placed a cap and a 30-day cool-off on submissions through its security portal, and anyone who wants to file more must make a special request. The change came because AI-powered finds had overwhelmed its review teams and were drowning out human researchers, the Financial Times reported.

The cost is concrete. Security firm Bynario found a high-severity macOS flaw that let a remote attacker create files as root, then run commands as root. It could not report the bug quickly. It had already hit Apple’s cap after filing 50 bugs in three weeks, it wrote.

Apple reached out directly and patched it. The twist: Bynario had found the bug using AI.

Google reprices the hard bugs

Google took a third path. It rebuilt its Android and Chrome reward rules. Now it pays top money for the hard, novel exploits AI still cannot produce, and less for the routine ones it now can. It is retiring bonuses for techniques that “AI has made almost routine,” it said. It also wants short, concrete reproducers rather than the long write-ups AI churns out.

The economics break

The common thread is money. Bug bounties were built around scarce human expertise, and AI has made both finding a bug and describing it cheap. The same slop is poisoning the public vulnerability database. AI is also finding real flaws at scale, and hunting bugs as fast as it files noise.

For defenders, the upside is real. An AI bug-hunter helped find a master key to every database in Microsoft’s Azure Cosmos DB. Anthropic’s Claude turned up flaws in cryptographic algorithms that experts had missed. The problem is telling that signal from the flood. Each of the big three has now picked a different way to try, and none of them looks final.

content_html_zh:
人工智能已经学会比人类更快地发现软件错误，而为这些错误付费的程序正在紧张。 在一周内，三个最大的公司走了三种不同的路。

微软支付了创纪录的金额。 苹果公司对研究人员可以提交多少错误关闭了大门。 谷歌悄悄地重新定价了整个事情。 这三个人都对同一场洪水做出了反应。

据 The Register 报道，微软在最近的赏金年度向 562 名研究人员支付了超过 2000 万美元，这两项奖金均创历史新高。 一年前，这个数字约为 1700 万美元，对 344 美元。 微软将这一激增归咎于安全研究中“人工智能的日益使用”。

但这并不是一个清晰的比较：该公司还在今年中期扩大了错误的范围。

苹果关上了门

苹果走了相反的路。 它对通过其安全门户提交的内容设置了上限和 30 天的冷静期，任何想要提交更多内容的人都必须提出特殊请求。 据英国《金融时报》报道，这一变化的发生是因为人工智能驱动的发现已经压垮了其审查团队，并淹没了人类研究人员。

成本是具体的。 安全公司 Bynario 发现了一个高严重性的 macOS 缺陷，该缺陷允许远程攻击者以 root 身份创建文件，然后以 root 身份运行命令。 它无法快速报告该错误。 它写道，在三周内提交了 50 个错误后，它已经达到了苹果的上限。

苹果直接伸出援手并修补了它。 变化是：Bynario 使用人工智能发现了该错误。

谷歌重新定价硬错误

谷歌走了第三条路。 它重建了 Android 和 Chrome 奖励规则。 现在，它为人工智能仍然无法产生的硬性、新颖的探索付出了高昂的代价，而为它现在可以产生的常规探索支付了更少的费用。 它表示，“人工智能几乎已经成为常态”的技术的奖金将被取消。 它还需要简短、具体的复制品，而不是人工智能产出的长篇文章。

经济崩溃

共同点是钱。 漏洞赏金是围绕稀缺的人类专业知识而建立的，而人工智能使得发现漏洞和描述它变得便宜。 同样的错误正在毒害公共漏洞数据库。 人工智能还大规模地发现真正的缺陷，并以与记录噪音一样快的速度寻找错误。

对于防守者来说，好处是真实的。 人工智能 bug 猎人帮助找到了 Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB 中每个数据库的主密钥。 Anthropic 的克劳德发现了专家们忽视的密码算法缺陷。 问题在于如何从洪水中辨别出这个信号。 三巨头现在都选择了不同的尝试方式，但没有一个看起来是最终的。
